governance_constraints.penalty_hint: Trust and renewal risk increase if violated.

governance_constraints.title: Margin preservation guardrail
governance_constraints.description: Do not run growth-heavy campaigns when ops margin is already below the board target.
governance_constraints.penalty_hint: Board pressure and cash efficiency worsen if violated.

backlog.title: Hire Support Ops
backlog.description: Add support operations and QA capacity to stabilize queue quality and automation coverage.
risk_notes: Support ops hires reduce fire drills but can be underutilized without workflow discipline.
Acts as a force multiplier when renewals or onboarding quality are already noisy.
backlog.impact_summary: The clearest visible win is steadier service outcomes. It looks most relevant for SMB, mid-market. The most exposed accounts right now are Atlas Capital Customer 7, Atlas Capital Customer 11. The first-order impact should show up quickly if rollout stays clean. Expect service-quality review from support leadership.

backlog.title: Hire Enterprise CSMs
backlog.description: Expand high-touch success coverage for renewal-sensitive and strategic accounts.
risk_notes: Coverage helps trust, but payback is slow unless renewals are genuinely at risk.
Works best when support quality stays high enough for CSM follow-through.
backlog.impact_summary: The clearest visible win is steadier service outcomes. It looks most relevant for mid-market, enterprise. The most exposed accounts right now are Atlas Capital Customer 7, Atlas Capital Customer 11. The first-order impact should show up quickly if rollout stays clean. The main watch-out is more coordination drag across teams.

backlog.title: Hire Growth Pod
backlog.description: Add PMM + growth engineering capacity to improve activation and acquisition throughput.
risk_notes: Hiring compounding GTM work pays off slowly and can spread product capacity thin.
Backfires if queue health and delivery reliability are already wobbling.
backlog.impact_summary: The clearest visible win is better activation and adoption. It looks most relevant for self-serve, SMB. The most exposed accounts right now are Atlas Capital Customer 7, Atlas Capital Customer 11. The first-order impact should show up quickly if rollout stays clean. The main watch-out is more delivery complexity.

backlog.title: Hire SRE Cluster
backlog.description: Expand reliability and platform operations capacity for cost and incident reduction.
risk_notes: Reliability hires compound over time and help most when burnout is already visible.
Best when leadership is willing to trade near-term growth optics for execution leverage.
backlog.impact_summary: The clearest visible win is better team throughput. It looks most relevant for enterprise, strategic accounts. The most exposed accounts right now are Atlas Capital Customer 7, Atlas Capital Customer 11. The first-order impact should show up quickly if rollout stays clean. The main watch-out is extra conversion risk during rollout. Execution risk looks comparatively contained. Expect margin review before rollout expands. Expect service-quality review from support leadership.

backlog.title: Hire Billing Ops
backlog.description: Increase monetization and packaging throughput through commercial operations support.
risk_notes: Commercial ops hires help expansion, but can backfire if trust is already fragile.
Visible upside is highest after renewal coverage is already credible.
backlog.impact_summary: The clearest visible win is stronger commercial follow-through. It looks most relevant for mid-market, enterprise. The most exposed accounts right now are Atlas Capital Customer 7, Atlas Capital Customer 11. The first-order impact should show up quickly if rollout stays clean. The main watch-out is a greater chance of customer pushback.

decision_ledger.rationale: The primary objective is to mitigate immediate renewal risks for high-value accounts (like acct 12) which are approaching critical windows. Given the high stakes of the current revenue base and the presence of significant renewal pressure, prioritizing stability and retention over aggressive expansion or new feature development is the most prudent way to protect the company's valuation and cash runway. This approach also aligns with the need to maintain the trust of key stakeholders (CEO/CFO) during a period of high-pressure renewals.

The most immediate and quantifiable risk to the business is the upcoming renewal of acct_012 in 12 days, which currently has a critically low health score of 0.35. While the compliance audit on March 8th represents a significant systemic risk to our 'trust' pillar, the imminent loss of a key account represents a direct and certain hit to MRR and retention metrics. Implementing a success plan now provides the necessary window to stabilize this account and prevent churn, while still leaving a small window to pivot toward audit preparation if the situation allows.

decision_ledger.rationale: The primary objective is to mitigate immediate renewal risks for high-value accounts (like acct 12) which are approaching critical windows. Given the high stakes of the current revenue base and the presence of significant renewal pressure, prioritizing stability and retention over aggressive expansion or new feature development is the most prudent way to protect the company's valuation and cash runway. This approach also aligns with the need to maintain the trust of key stakeholders (CEO/CFO) during a period of high-pressure renewals.

The most immediate and quantifiable risk to the business is the upcoming renewal of acct_012 in 12 days, which currently has a critically low health score of 0.35. While the compliance audit on March 8th represents a significant systemic risk to our 'trust' pillar, the imminent loss of a key account represents a direct and certain hit to MRR and retention metrics. Implementing a success plan now provides the necessary window to stabilize this account and prevent churn, while still leaving a small window to pivot toward audit preparation if the situation allows.

decision_ledger.rationale: The primary objective is to mitigate immediate renewal risks for high-value accounts (like acct 12) which are approaching critical windows. Given the high stakes of the current revenue base and the presence of significant renewal pressure, prioritizing stability and retention over aggressive expansion or new feature development is the most prudent way to protect the company's valuation and cash runway. This approach also aligns with the need to maintain the trust of key stakeholders (CEO/CFO) during a period of high-pressure renewals.

The most immediate and quantifiable risk to the business is the upcoming renewal of acct_012 in 12 days, which currently has a critically low health score of 0.35. While the compliance audit on March 8th represents a significant systemic risk to our 'trust' pillar, the imminent loss of a key account represents a direct and certain hit to MRR and retention metrics. Implementing a success plan now provides the necessary window to stabilize this account and prevent churn, while still leaving a small window to pivot toward audit preparation if the situation allows.
